newsitem.title: FRANCE: France may look at company tax breaks in 98 - finmin.
newsitem.headline: France may look at company tax breaks in 98 - finmin.

text.p: France may introduce tax breaks next year for companies possibly planning on hiring workers or investing, Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said in an interview with the Financial Times published on Tuesday.

"It is not impossible that next year we will put in place ways for companies to free themselves from some corporate taxes, based on commitments in certain areas -- maybe investment, maybe on hiring," the newspaper quoted him as saying.
Strauss-Kahn on Monday announced a 15 percent surcharge on company profits and a rise in capital gains tax to raise revenues to cut France's budget deficit in preparation for European monetary union.
